faq.name: Can my boss do that? – Apprentice Rights Checker
faq.description: Interactive rights checker for trainees and apprentices in Germany, with scenarios on overtime, holiday, dismissal, vocational school and more.

mainEntity.name: Can my boss order me to work overtime as an apprentice?

acceptedAnswer.text: As a rule, no. Apprentices who are minors may work a maximum of 8 hours/day and 40 hours/week (§ 8 JArbSchG). For apprentices of legal age, the Working Hours Act applies. Overtime must be paid or compensated with time off (§ 17 (3) BBiG).

mainEntity.name: Can my boss cancel my holiday as an apprentice?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Once approved, holiday can only be revoked in absolute exceptional cases. Apprentices who are minors are entitled to 25–30 working days/year (§ 19 JArbSchG), adults at least 24 working days (§ 3 BUrlG).

mainEntity.name: Do I have to clean and sweep the hall as an apprentice?

acceptedAnswer.text: Only in moderation. Apprentices may only be assigned tasks that serve the purpose of the training (§ 14 BBiG). Occasionally tidying your own workstation is fine; regularly cleaning the company is an impermissible non-training activity.

mainEntity.name: Do I have to go in to work after vocational school?

acceptedAnswer.text: Apprentices who are minors with more than 5 lessons on a single day are fully released (§ 9 JArbSchG). Vocational-school time counts towards working time (§ 15 BBiG).

mainEntity.name: Can my boss dismiss me as an apprentice after the probationary period?

acceptedAnswer.text: Only for good cause and without notice (§ 22 BBiG). Ordinary termination by the company is not possible after the probationary period. A warning is usually required beforehand.

mainEntity.name: Do I have to use my holiday for the exam?

acceptedAnswer.text: No! You have a statutory right to paid release for exams and the day before (§ 15 BBiG). This may not be credited against your holiday.

mainEntity.name: Does my trainer have to provide tools and work materials?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. The training company is obliged to provide training materials free of charge – tools, materials, specialist books and any prescribed work clothing (§ 14 (1) no. 3 BBiG).
